Cook's tenure as Apple CEO is just weeks away from ending, with John Ternus set to take over the top job on September 1. Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan believes Ternus could usher in a bigger, bolder new era for Apple.

Under John Ternus, more new products, acquisitions, and R&D investment are expected, showing greater drive

Apple's CEO transition is nearly complete. So far, the company has gone to great lengths to emphasise the continuity Ternus will bring to the role.

However, not everyone on Wall Street is convinced Ternus will stick quite so closely to Cook's playbook.

In a research note obtained by The Street, Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan reiterated a strong 'buy' rating on Apple, with one of the recommendations' key points being the expectation that Ternus will continue Cook's legacy while having a greater 'risk appetite'. Moz Farooque wrote:

The bank highlighted that Apple abandoning its net-cash-neutral target is an early signal that management may be more willing to deploy capital. This would translate into higher R&D spending, more capital expenditure (CapEx), and potentially larger deals—areas that were not central features of Cook's strategy. Under Ternus, BofA believes Apple could move more quickly into a number of brand-new product categories, including AI glasses, AirPods with cameras, smart rings, smart home, Personal Assistant, and robotics.

Ultimately, BofA believes Ternus will continue Cook's legacy of building Apple into a highly profitable global enterprise, but also expects him to leverage the company's current strong position to make bolder moves going forward.

With Ternus just taking the CEO helm, we may not see any major changes right away. However, in the coming months, any potential shifts in priorities may begin to come into clearer view.

What are your expectations for John Ternus as Apple CEO? Let us know in the comments.
